newsitem.title: UK: Asia funds look to cut Hong Kong exposure - survey.
newsitem.headline: Asia funds look to cut Hong Kong exposure - survey.

text.p: Asia Pacific fund managers are looking to reduce their holdings in Hong Kong equities amid concerns about the outlook for the property sector, a survey by Merrill Lynch said.

The survey of Asia Pacific fund managers found sellers outnumbered buyers by 25 percent -- the first time managers were looking to reduce exposure in Hong Kong equities since the survey began in April.
Merrill global strategist Bijal Shah said there had been an increase in the number of directors of Hong Kong companies selling stock over the last two months.
"This shows that the market is very highly valued and a number of fund managers are looking to reduce their exposure. The market is very susceptible to bad news," he said.
The survey said property was the least liked sector in the region.
Bullishness about the global economy had raised buying interest in South Korean equities due to its dominant manufacturing sector, the survey said.
It said fund in the region were most bearish on the outlook for the Malaysian equity market, where sellers outnumbered buyers by 50 percent.
The survey, conducted by Gallup, covered 12 leading institutions in the region managing funds totalling $236 billion.
